newsitem.title: USA: Weak NYMEX crude pressures some U.S. spot resids.
newsitem.headline: Weak NYMEX crude pressures some U.S. spot resids.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to down slightly Tuesday in sluggish trade, with a sharp selloff in NYMEX crude and mild East Coast weather still undermining the complex, industry sources said.

"I thought we were stable until crude sold off, but the weather is not too conducive for air conditioning anyway," said one cash trader, noting buyers backed off today as NYMEX crude prices crumbled more than 60 cents.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to about $16.25 a barrel, with July paper off a quarter or more to the $16.25-50 area with softer crude, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour again notionally eased a quarter to $16.75-17.00.
High sulphurs in New York held relatively steady, with 2.2 percent still talked in the low-$15s, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was quoted slightly lower at $16.00-25, while three percent was unchanged at $14.25-50.
USG July three percent paper was pegged on either side of $14.50, also little changed on the day.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate gas prices slipped more than a nickel Tuesday to the high-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.99 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was almost a dime lower at about $2.12/mmBtu, or $13.36 a barrel.
